title: Entitlement decision fabric and runtime admission hub
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a unified entitlement decision fabric and a lightweight runtime admission hub that sits inline with API, runtime, and Console traffic. The goal is to replace ad-hoc RBAC checks spread across services with a single decision pathway that: 1) evaluates structured entitlement policies (RBAC v2 DSL), 2) emits consistent audit events, 3) applies admission controls (allow/deny/rate-limit/deny-with-reason), and 4) provides fast local fallback via a compact decision cache. This ticket covers the core engine and the middleware shim for Gateway/API, serving runtime, and Console routes. It also includes SSO/SAML attribute mapping hooks and an audit-event canonicalizer so downstream sinks (BigQuery/Elasticsearch) receive normalized events.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime admission hub deployed as a low-latency middleware for API and Console paths with end-to-end median added latency < 7ms under p95 load
Entitlement decision fabric evaluates RBAC v2 rules and returns explicit allow/deny with reason and enforcement metadata
Local decision cache supports TTL and revocation; cache hit should reduce average decision time by >= 65% for steady-state workloads
Audit events emitted for every evaluated request with canonical fields (actor, resource, action, decision, rule_id, trace_id, timestamp) and sent to audit-sink staging cluster
SSO/SAML mapping layer can extract group and role assertions and map them to internal principal attributes used in RBAC v2 rules
Console admin controls surface the last-evaluated rule and human-readable enforcement reason in the UI for authorized auditors
Automated tests covering policy edge-cases (deny overrides, attribute-dependent rules, nested resources) and integration tests exercising cache revocation and fallback to central PDP
Canary rollout plan defined with metrics and automatic rollback triggers (error rate, auth latency, increase in 5xxs, audit-event loss)
implementation_notes: Decision fabric will expose gRPC and HTTP/JSON adapters; prefer gRPC for internal high-throughput paths and HTTP for Console/UI
Use a compact in-memory decision cache keyed by stable principal/resource/action tuple with LRU and explicit invalidation via revocation topic on Kafka
Policy evaluation engine will compile RBAC v2 DSL into an optimized decision DAG; include a debug mode that returns the matched rule path for observability
Audit canonicalizer will map provider-specific attributes (SAML NameID, OIDC claims) into the canonical actor/resource/action schema before emitting
Fallback behavior: on PDP timeout or evaluator panic, middleware applies configurable fail-open or fail-closed policy per route/team with safe defaults = fail-closed for console-admin routes
Integrate with existing token tracing (trace_id) so authorization decisions are correlated with request traces in Tempo/Jaeger
Expose per-decision telemetry (latency, cache_hit, rule_id, size_of_principal_attrs) to Console and to internal metrics pipeline
Security: ensure the middleware sanitizes inputs to the policy engine to avoid injection via crafted attributes and maintain a whitelist of allowed attribute keys
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit + integration tests in CI; run static policy fuzzer for 48h against new compiler
Stage 1: Deploy to staging with real traffic replay; validate audit shape and latency budgets
Stage 2: Canary to 5% of production API traffic and Console read-only routes for 72h; monitor auth latency p95, error ratio, and missing audit events
Stage 3: Expand to 50% with policy shadowing for crash scenarios; enable revocation testing
Stage 4: Full roll with automatic rollback if auth-error-rate > 0.5% or audit loss detected > 1% for 15m
tests_and_eval: Unit tests for compiler transformations and DAG evaluation correctness
Property-based tests for policy equivalence (old engine vs new fabric) on a corpus of production policies
Load test: simulate 10k rps with realistic mix of short-lived and long-lived sessions; verify median decision latency and p95 under cache hit/miss
Chaos test: inject PDP latency and assert middleware fallback behavior conforms to route config
Audit pipeline verification: end-to-end validation that canonical audit events land in staging BigQuery within 30s
comments: 2025-11-10 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after architecture sync. Goal is to consolidate scattered checks into a single admission pathway. Assigned to Jordan.
2025-11-13 Jordan Patel: Spike completed. Verified a prototype gRPC evaluator with a simple compiled policy DAG. Observed ~9ms median with no cache on devbox; adding cache reduced median to ~2.5ms.
2025-11-17 Security review (K. Alvarez): Requesting explicit threat model for attribute injection and revocation attacks. Also require KMS-backed signing for policy bundle manifests.
2025-11-19 Design feedback (L. Fischer): Console should present a human-friendly rule explanation; propose a short phrase + link to matched policy line.
2025-11-22 Jordan Patel: Implemented audit canonicalizer and Kafka revocation topic. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/612. Requesting review from runtime and console owners.
